rows.meaning: sole; sole one in a category
rows.note: Use 唯一 as the all-purpose adjective for a sole member of a category, and for the sole child of a particular sex, such as an only son even if there are daughters.

example.english: She is the only female engineer in the whole company.
example.traditional: 佢係成間公司唯一嘅女工程師。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 seng4 gaan1 gung1 si1 wai4 jat1 ge3 neoi5 gung1 cing4 si1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for excluding others or limiting the amount to a stated number.

example.english: I only want to have a cup of tea.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zing6 hai6 soeng2 jam2 bui1 caa4

rows.note: Use 獨生 before 仔, 女, or 子女 when the child has no siblings at all.

example.english: I’m an only child, so I had no brothers or sisters growing up.
example.traditional: 我係獨生仔，細個冇兄弟姊妹。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai6 duk6 sang1 zai2 sai3 go3 mou5 hing1 dai6 zi2 mui6

rows.note: Use this before an unexpected or disappointing result corresponding to English “only to.”

example.english: I left home early on purpose, only to get stuck in traffic anyway.
example.traditional: 我特登早啲出門口，點知仲係塞車。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dak6 dang1 zou2 di1 ceot1 mun4 hau2 dim2 zi1 zung6 hai6 sak1 ce1

rows.note: Use this for the “merely” or “no more than” sense when downplaying what is being described.

example.english: This is only a small problem.
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 bat1 gwo3 hai6 siu2 man6 tai4

rows.note: Use this specifically when “only” means that something happened just recently.

example.jyutping: ngo5 ngaam1 ngaam1 sin1 sik6 jyun4 faan6
